hub.title: K-Culture Rankings
hub.metaTitle: K-pop, K-drama and Korean actor rankings, updated daily
hub.metaDescription: Daily buzz charts for K-pop, Korean actors and K-dramas, calculated from Korean community data and Wikipedia interest in 8 languages. Free to reuse under CC BY 4.0.
hub.lead: Calculated every morning from what Korea is talking about and what the world is looking up. No paid votes.
hub.dataBody: Reuse any chart under CC BY 4.0 with credit to Unnie Note. The last 90 days as JSON or CSV:

method.title: How the rankings work
method.metaDescription: How Unnie Note calculates its daily K-pop, actor and K-drama buzz charts: signals, weights, entry rules, sources and licenses.
method.intro: Every chart is calculated by code from public data, not by editors or AI. The same data always gives the same ranking.
method.kr: Korea buzz (KR) adds up 7 days of theqoo hot-board views and comments, Google Trends KR searches and Yonhap news mentions.
method.gl: Global interest (GL) averages 7-day Wikipedia page views across 8 languages, so English Wikipedia can’t dominate the score.
method.score: The final score gives the two halves equal weight.
method.normalize: Every signal is log-scaled, then rescaled to 0–100 within that day’s candidates.
method.types: Candidates are filtered by their Wikidata type: groups and singers for K-pop, actors for the actors chart, series for K-dramas. A comedian can’t land in the K-pop chart.
method.entry: To be ranked, a candidate needs at least one Korean signal in the last 7 days and a Wikipedia article in at least one language.
method.rising: Climbing 5 or more places within the top 30 counts as rising. NEW means the candidate wasn’t on the previous chart.
method.local: “Rising in your language” ranks the growth of Wikipedia views in that language (this week vs last week, at least 500 views).
method.fans: Fan cheers are shown separately and never change the score. The weekly fan vote is a chart of its own.
